types.name: Identifier
types.description: An external or natural key. `system` is a registered scheme (email, domain, vat:eu, sha256, stripe:customer, postware:workspace).

types.name: ContactPoint
types.description: One email, phone or URL; used by the emails[], phones[] and urls[] arrays.

fields.name: country
fields.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2

fields.name: currency
fields.description: ISO 4217

types.name: Status
types.description: category is the standard (validated per model); state is the workspace's own label.

types.name: Affiliation
types.description: A person's membership of an organization; the job title lives on the Person.

fields.name: rrule
fields.description: RFC 5545 RRULE

fields.name: where
fields.description: a query grammar `where` object

types.name: Participant
types.description: A person or address taking part in a message or an event (an RFC 5322 mailbox, a JMAP EmailAddress, an iCalendar ATTENDEE or ORGANIZER). Every field is optional; ref names the Person or Member when one is known, address carries the email, phone number or handle as the channel wrote it.

fields.name: address
fields.description: email address, phone number or handle, as the channel writes it

fields.name: role
fields.description: events: required, optional or resource (iCalendar ROLE and CUTYPE)

fields.name: status
fields.description: events: the participation status (iCalendar PARTSTAT)

models.name: identity
models.title: Identity
models.description: How a principal authenticates: a provider's stable subject bound to a Member (an operator) or a Person (an end user), with the asserted email and the kinds of factor used. Credential material lives in the auth store, never here.
models.agent_context:
Identity is written by the auth component when someone signs in; you never create or edit one. A Person with an
Identity is an end user. Dedupe by (provider, subject); an email is never an Identity key, only a Person one.
The one mistake: looking for passwords or tokens here; credentials are never stored on records.

fields.name: principal
fields.description: operator or end user

fields.name: provider
fields.description: builtin, or the issuer URL of an external provider

fields.name: subject
fields.description: the provider's stable id (OIDC sub)

fields.name: email
fields.description: the address this login asserts; never a key

fields.name: factors
fields.description: the kinds of credential used; device and enrolment details live in the auth store

fields.name: claims
fields.description: mapped provider claims; never tokens

fields.name: last_seen_at
fields.description: touched at most once an hour; drives the monthly active user count

models.name: import_run
models.title: Import run
models.description: One execution of an importer: which importer, in which mode, with what outcome and per-model counts. Every record it wrote carries its id in source.import_run.
models.agent_context:
An ImportRun is created by import_run or `a import`, never by hand; read it for the counts and the errors, and
always run with dry_run first. Find what a run wrote by querying source.import_run. The one mistake: retrying a
partial run without reading its errors; the rows that succeeded are already upserted and simply update again.

fields.name: importer
fields.description: csv, stripe, supabase, ...

fields.name: counts
fields.description: per model: {created, updated, skipped, errors}

fields.name: row
fields.description: the source row, 1-based, header excluded

fields.name: path
fields.description: the field path that failed

models.name: member
models.title: Member
models.description: An operator of the workspace: a person on the team, an agent or a service, with roles. Authorization, audit and the owner and assignee fields point at Members.
models.agent_context:
Member is who operates the workspace, including you: an agent runs as the Member its API key was created for.
End users of the product are never Members; they are Persons with an Identity, and a guest is a Person with a
Share, not a role. Dedupe by person, or by the invitation email while invited. The one mistake: creating a
Member to represent a customer or a contact; create a Person instead.

fields.name: person
fields.description: the operator's own Person record

fields.name: roles
fields.description: owner, admin, member, or a custom role name that policies grant

fields.name: invitation
fields.description: set while status is invited; the magic link sent to this email activates the Member

models.name: policy
models.title: Policy
models.description: A rule: which principals may do which actions on which model, narrowed by a filter in the query grammar. Packs ship defaults, admins edit them, Shares compile into them.
models.agent_context:
Policies are ANDed into every read and write by end users, guests and the public; members are governed by roles
and never consult them. Only admins write Policies. Dedupe by name. The one mistake: a `where` written against
fields the model in applies_to does not have; run it as a query first.

fields.name: principal
value
fields.description: the role name for role, the share id for share
the class of caller the policy applies to

fields.name: applies_to
fields.description: a model name, or * for every model

fields.name: where
fields.description: a where object of the query grammar; variables @principal.person, @principal.member, @principal.identity, @principal.affiliated_organizations, @share.id, @now

fields.name: fields
fields.description: field allow-list for read or update

fields.name: origin
fields.description: who created it

models.name: share
models.title: Share
models.description: A grant of read, and optionally comment, access to records, by ids or by filter, to someone outside the workspace: a link, an email, another workspace or the public. Compiles into Policies for a synthetic principal.
models.agent_context:
Share is how records leave the workspace without being copied. Content is published by the Content pack's public
policy (a Collection with public: true), the same shape a public Share compiles to. Scope by filter when the set
changes over time, by ids when it is fixed. Comment is granted to email grantees only: a Note has an author. A link token is returned once at creation and lives in the credential store, never on the record.
The one mistake: deleting a Share to revoke it; set status to revoked, which keeps the audit trail.

fields.name: scope
fields.description: by ids or by filter

fields.name: grantee
fields.description: link, email, workspace or public

models.name: tag
models.title: Tag
models.description: A label that works the same on every record: a namespaced slug with a display name, a colour and a description. The envelope's tags[] holds slugs that resolve to Tag records.
models.agent_context:
Tags classify; they never carry meaning the standard depends on (that is a field or a Status). Write slugs in
tags[] on any record and missing workspace tags are created for you; create a Tag record only to set a colour or
a description. A slug is [namespace:]segment(/segment)*, each segment [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}, at most 255
characters, compared case-insensitively; name is the display form. Dedupe by (namespace, slug). The one mistake:
writing into a reserved namespace (sys, a pack name, a source name); those belong to the server, packs and importers.

fields.name: name
fields.description: the display form; may carry case and spaces

fields.name: slug
fields.description: lowercase segments joined by /

fields.name: namespace
fields.description: none = workspace-local; sys, a pack name and a source name are reserved

fields.name: color
fields.description: #RRGGBB

fields.name: applies_to
fields.description: model names this tag is meant for; absent means any

models.name: workspace
models.title: Workspace
models.description: The tenant: one company or one person, holding exactly one of these records, its first. Holds the installed packs and the members, identities, policies, shares, tags and records.
models.agent_context:
Workspace is the tenant. You never create one; provisioning does, and a workspace holds exactly one of these
records. Read it for the installed packs and the sign-in settings. Dedupe by slug. The one mistake: updating auth
without reading it first; the object is replaced whole on update.

fields.name: slug
fields.description: URL-safe, unique per server or platform

fields.name: packs
fields.description: installed packs

fields.name: auth
allowed_email_domains
fields.description: when set, only these domains may sign up as end users

fields.name: allowed_redirect_uris
fields.description: redirect URIs the magic-link and OAuth flows may return to; localhost is always allowed

fields.name: allowed_origins
fields.description: CORS origins

fields.name: signup
fields.description: whether an unknown email may create an end user

fields.name: issuers
claims
fields.description: which claim carries each value

fields.name: member_role_claim_values
fields.description: role name to claim value, for member issuers

fields.name: auto_join
fields.description: for member issuers: add anyone the issuer vouches for as a Member; off means invited or bound people only
external OIDC issuers this workspace trusts
sign-in settings

models.name: event
models.title: Event
models.description: A scheduled block of time: a meeting, a call, an appointment, a reminder. One record per series; a logged call or meeting is an Event too.
models.agent_context:
Event is anything with a time slot, past or future; the timeline of a Deal or a Ticket is a query over the Events,
Messages, Notes and Tasks about it. Give a recurring Event its IANA timezone so local times survive daylight
saving; one Recurrence rule per series, exceptions are ext.calendar.*. Dedupe by the iCalendar uid identifier
(system ical:uid). The one mistake: an attendee as free text when a Person or Member exists; set attendees[].ref.

fields.name: period
fields.description: start inclusive; end exclusive, omitted for a zero-duration event

fields.name: timezone
fields.description: IANA zone of start and end

models.name: file
models.title: File
models.description: Stored or referenced binary content with a name and a type. The bytes live in object storage or on disk; the record holds the name, type, size and location.
models.agent_context:
Create a File through the upload flow (upload-url, then complete), not by hand, so the storage key and the sha256
identifier are right. Dedupe by identifier: the server adds {system: sha256} for stored bytes; sources may add
md5, sha1, crc32, quickxor or dropbox:content-hash, and <source>:file for their own ids. The one mistake: a URL to
an external file stored as a File; a File is bytes the workspace holds or a source system stores.

fields.name: mime_type
fields.description: detected by the server; importers fall back to the extension or application/octet-stream

fields.name: size
fields.description: bytes; absent for native cloud documents

fields.name: provider
fields.description: local, s3, or a source system

models.name: message
models.title: Message
models.description: One message on a channel: an email, a chat message, an SMS, a call record, with sender, recipients, body and the records it is about. A Ticket's conversation is its Messages.
models.agent_context:
Message is a communication that happened or will be sent; internal commentary is a Note. Link it to the Ticket or
Deal through about and to its thread through thread_key. Dedupe by identifier: email:message-id (the Message-ID
without angle brackets) for mail, slack:ts for chat, <source>:message otherwise. The one mistake: setting
delivery on an inbound Message; delivery describes outbound sending.

fields.name: body
fields.description: plain text or Markdown; may be empty when the message is only attachments

fields.name: thread_key
fields.description: opaque grouping key: a mail thread id, a chat channel and thread, a ticket id

fields.name: delivery
fields.description: outbound only

fields.name: about
fields.description: the Ticket, the Deal

models.name: note
models.title: Note
models.description: Free text about one or more records: an internal note, a comment, a meeting summary. A Note about exactly one record is a comment on it.
models.agent_context:
Note is the only place for commentary; a conversation with a customer is Messages. Always set about (the records
it concerns) and author. Dedupe by identifier only. The one mistake: visibility shared on a Note meant for the
team; shared Notes are readable by the end users who can read the record they are about.

fields.name: body
fields.description: Markdown

fields.name: author
fields.description: a guest's comment is a Note by a Person

fields.name: about
fields.description: one record makes it a comment; several make a CRM note

models.name: organization
models.title: Organization
models.description: A company, nonprofit, government body or household: a customer, a vendor, a partner or an account. The relationship to the workspace lives on Deals, Invoices, affiliations and tags, never on the Organization.
models.agent_context:
Use Organization for any company or institution. Dedupe by the domain identifier (identifiers [{system: domain,
value: ...}]); derive the domain from a website URL before creating, and add vat:*, duns or lei identifiers when
known. Firmographics (industry, employees, annual revenue) are ext.crm.*, the registered name for invoices is
ext.billing.legal_name, and the relationship (customer, partner, vendor) is a tag. The one mistake: a second
Organization for the same company under another spelling of its name.

fields.name: urls
fields.description: website first; social profiles after

fields.name: addresses
fields.description: kind billing, shipping, mailing, work or other

models.name: person
models.title: Person
models.description: A human being: a customer, a contact, an employee, or an end user of the product.
models.agent_context:
Use Person for any human, whatever their role. Roles live on relationships (affiliations, Deal.people,
Ticket.requester), never on the Person; a lead is a Person with ext.crm.lifecycle_stage lead. Dedupe by email:
before creating, query by emails.value or use upsert. An end user of the product is a Person that holds an
Identity; you never create Identities yourself. The one mistake: a second Person for the same human under another
email; add the address to emails[] instead.

fields.name: phones
fields.description: label mobile, home, fax, work or other

fields.name: urls
fields.description: websites and social profiles; the URL identifies the network

fields.name: affiliations
fields.description: Organizations this person belongs to, with role, primary flag and period

fields.name: locale
fields.description: BCP 47; the OIDC locale claim

fields.name: timezone
fields.description: IANA zone; the OIDC zoneinfo claim

models.name: product
models.title: Product
models.description: A thing the business sells or buys: a good, a service or a digital item. What it costs lives on a Price in the Billing pack.
models.agent_context:
One Product per sellable thing, never one per price: the amount, currency and billing interval live on Prices
that reference it, and a plan billed monthly and yearly is one Product with two Prices. Dedupe by the sku
identifier (system sku). Inventory counts, purchase cost and ledger accounts are extensions. The one mistake:
deleting a Product that Invoices or Subscriptions reference; set active to false instead.

fields.name: unit
fields.description: default unit of measure for invoice lines: a UN/ECE Rec 20 code (C62, HUR) or a word (seat, hour)

fields.name: tax_rate
fields.description: the default tax rate for lines of this product

models.name: project
models.title: Project
models.description: A container of work with a lifecycle: planned, active, paused, done or cancelled. Tasks belong to it.
models.agent_context:
Project is the container Tasks belong to; link it to what it is for through about (the client Organization, the
Deal). Dedupe by identifier only, so check for an existing Project by name before creating one. archived_at
hides it from default views and is independent of status. The one mistake: marking a Project done while Tasks
in it are still open.

fields.name: archived_at
fields.description: hidden from default views; independent of status

fields.name: about
fields.description: the client, the deal

models.name: task
models.title: Task
models.description: A unit of work with a status, a priority, assignees and a due date. It nests under a parent Task and belongs to one Project.
models.agent_context:
Task is work someone has to do; a reminder at a time is an Event, a request from a customer is a Ticket. Use
due_on for a date and due_at only when the source has a time of day. Blocked is a state label under open or
in_progress, not a category. Dedupe by identifier only, so search open Tasks by title before creating one.
The one mistake: setting status.category to done without completed_at; set both.

fields.name: due_at
fields.description: set only when the source has a time of day

models.name: team
models.title: Team
models.description: A named group of Members that work is assigned to.
models.agent_context:
Team groups Members of this workspace (operators), not Persons; a customer's departments are Organizations with a
parent. Dedupe by a source identifier, then by name. Hierarchy, group type and a lead are ext.org.*; the
accountable operator is the envelope's owner. The one mistake: adding a Person to members; only Members belong.

models.name: deal
models.title: Deal
models.description: A potential sale to an Organization or a Person, tracked through a Pipeline, with an amount, a probability and an expected close. Won or lost is the status category.
models.agent_context:
Deal is the opportunity, not the customer: the customer is the Organization or Person it points at. Set stage
to a key of its Pipeline; status.category follows that stage's category unless you set it (a deal can be lost
from any stage), and won emits deal.won. people[] holds the contacts on the deal, one marked primary. Dedupe by
identifier only, so query open Deals for the same Organization before creating one. The one mistake: products,
quantities and prices on the Deal; they belong on the quote or the Invoice.

fields.name: role
fields.description: e.g. decision maker, billing contact

fields.name: stage
fields.description: a stage key of the pipeline

fields.name: status
fields.description: category defaults from the stage's category

fields.name: probability
fields.description: 0 to 1; defaults from the stage

fields.name: closed_at
fields.description: set when status.category leaves open

models.name: pipeline
models.title: Pipeline
models.description: An ordered set of stages that Deals move through, each mapped to one of the standard categories open, won or lost. A workspace has one default pipeline.
models.agent_context:
Read the default pipeline before creating a Deal and use one of its stage keys; Deal.pipeline is required and
the default pipeline is used when you omit it. Every pipeline holds at least one open, one won and one lost
stage. Dedupe by name. The one mistake: deleting or re-keying a stage that Deals reference; set archived true
and keep the key.

fields.name: default
fields.description: the pipeline new Deals go to when none is given

fields.name: key
fields.description: stable, snake_case; referenced by Deal.stage

fields.name: probability
fields.description: 0 to 1; the default for Deal.probability

fields.name: archived
fields.description: retired; kept because Deals still reference it

models.name: invoice
models.title: Invoice
models.description: A statement of money owed for goods or services: receivable when we issued it, payable when we received it (a bill). Lines with amounts and taxes, totals, a status from draft to paid, and the payments applied to it.
models.agent_context:
Create with status draft; number may be empty until the invoice leaves draft, then it is required and unique per
workspace for receivable invoices and per counterparty for payable ones. subtotal is the sum of lines.amount,
total is subtotal minus discount_total plus tax_total (tax_total excluded when tax_inclusive), amount_due is
total minus amount_paid (zero on a void invoice); overdue and partially paid are queries, not statuses. The one mistake: status paid
without a Payment; create the Payment, apply it, then set paid and paid_at, which emits invoice.paid.

fields.name: number
fields.description: required once status is not draft; unique per workspace when receivable, per counterparty when payable

fields.name: direction
fields.description: a bill is a payable Invoice

fields.name: bill_to
fields.description: the billing address as printed; defaults from the counterparty

fields.name: due_at
fields.description: due_at or terms is given when amount_due is above zero

fields.name: terms
fields.description: payment terms as text, e.g. Net 30

fields.name: currency
fields.description: ISO 4217; every Money on the invoice uses it

fields.name: unit
fields.description: unit of measure; a UN/ECE Rec 20 code or a word

fields.name: discount
fields.description: line-level discount already deducted from amount

fields.name: amount
fields.description: quantity times unit_price minus discount; includes tax only when tax_inclusive

fields.name: period
fields.description: the service period the line covers

fields.name: subtotal
fields.description: the sum of lines.amount

fields.name: discount_total
fields.description: document-level discount

fields.name: amount_paid
fields.description: maintained from applied Payments

fields.name: amount_due
fields.description: total minus amount_paid

fields.name: reference
fields.description: the buyer's PO or reference

fields.name: memo
fields.description: a customer-facing note printed on the invoice

fields.name: about
fields.description: the Deal, the Project

models.name: payment
models.title: Payment
models.description: Money that moved against invoices: a customer paying us (receivable), us paying a vendor (payable), or a refund of either.
models.agent_context:
direction is the ledger side; kind says whether money went the normal way (payment) or back (refund, with
refund_of pointing at the original). applied[] says which Invoices this payment settles and by how much; update
their amount_paid and status yourself. Payments recorded from accounting systems are succeeded; processor payments
carry pending, failed or cancelled. Dedupe by identifier (the processor's or ledger's id). The one mistake: a
refund as a negative amount; record a Payment of kind refund.

fields.name: reference
fields.description: check number, bank reference, processor id or remittance text

models.name: price
models.title: Price
models.description: An amount at which a Product is sold, once or on a recurring interval. Subscription items and Invoice lines point at Prices.
models.agent_context:
interval one_time is a one-off price; any other interval with interval_count makes it recurring (month with
interval_count 3 bills quarterly). Metered usage, tiers and trials are ext.billing.*. Dedupe by an identifier
(the billing provider's price id) or by (product, name). The one mistake: changing the amount of a Price that
Subscriptions use; create a new Price and set active false on the old one.

fields.name: name
fields.description: a short label: Monthly, Annual, 2 seats

fields.name: amount
fields.description: per unit, per interval; tax per tax_inclusive

fields.name: interval_count
fields.description: intervals between charges; 3 with month bills quarterly

models.name: subscription
models.title: Subscription
models.description: A recurring agreement to bill (receivable) or be billed (payable) for Prices, period after period. Each period's charge is an Invoice that points back at it.
models.agent_context:
Subscription is the recurring relationship; each period's charge is an Invoice that references it. status pending
means it exists but has not started, so current_period and started_at are absent; cancel_at set means it will
not renew; ended_at is when it stopped. Dedupe by identifier (the billing provider's subscription id). The one
mistake: cancelled without ended_at and cancel_at; the dates are what the status means.

fields.name: direction
fields.description: receivable = our customer; payable = a vendor we pay

fields.name: current_period
fields.description: the period being billed now; absent while pending

fields.name: cancel_at
fields.description: scheduled end; when set the subscription does not renew

fields.name: reference
fields.description: the customer's PO or reference, copied onto generated invoices

models.name: tax_rate
models.title: Tax rate
models.description: A named tax percentage applied to invoice lines (VAT 20%, GST 5%, a state sales tax), referenced by Products and Invoice lines.
models.agent_context:
One TaxRate per rate you charge, referenced from Invoice lines; rate is the total percentage applied to a line,
and compound components, jurisdictions and tax kinds are ext.billing.*. Dedupe by a source identifier, then by
name. The one mistake: editing a rate that past Invoices reference when the law changes; create a new TaxRate
and set active false on the old one.

fields.name: rate
fields.description: percent: 20 means 20%

models.name: ticket
models.title: Ticket
models.description: A request for help from a Person, owned by the team until it is solved. The conversation is Messages about it; internal notes are Notes about it.
models.agent_context:
Ticket is the request; what was said is Messages with about [ticket], and what the team thinks is Notes about it.
Assignment and status changes are the audit log, not records. The requester is a Person, often an end user of the
product. Dedupe by the source system's id in identifiers, so search open Tickets from the same requester before
creating one. The one mistake: solved without a Message to the requester; solved emits ticket.solved.

fields.name: description
fields.description: the request as written; importers copy the first inbound message when the source has no description

fields.name: requester
fields.description: often the product's own end user

fields.name: resolved_at
fields.description: first time status became solved or closed

models.name: collection
models.title: Collection
models.description: A set of Documents published together: a site, a blog, a docs tree, a changelog or a help centre, with a slug and a public flag that publishes its published Documents.
models.agent_context:
Collection is the publication unit; public true makes every Document in it with status published, and a
published_at that has passed, readable without sign-in. Dedupe by slug. The one mistake: assuming drafts leak
when a Collection is public; only published Documents are served, but check its Documents before flipping it.

fields.name: public
fields.description: makes its published Documents publicly readable through the Content pack's public policy

models.name: document
models.title: Document
models.description: One piece of content in a Collection: a page, a post, a docs article, a changelog entry or a help article, in Markdown, with a status from draft to published, authors, SEO metadata and an optional parent for hierarchies.
models.agent_context:
Document is Markdown content with a workflow; publishing is status.category published inside a public Collection,
which emits document.published. A future published_at schedules: the public reads it only once that time has
passed. Dedupe by slug within the collection and locale. The one mistake: changing the slug of a published
Document; the slug is its URL.

fields.name: body
fields.description: Markdown; a source's native rich text stays in source.payload

fields.name: published_at
fields.description: set by the server on the first transition to published when absent; a future value schedules

fields.name: authors
fields.description: at least one

fields.name: locale
fields.description: BCP 47

fields.name: parent
fields.description: docs hierarchy

extensions.name: exchange_rate
extensions.description: The rate from the invoice currency to the workspace's reporting currency at issue, as a decimal string.

extensions.name: jurisdiction
extensions.description: Where the rate applies: { country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), region }.

extensions.name: legal_name
extensions.description: The registered legal name, when it differs from name; printed on invoices and used by the e-invoicing profile.

extensions.name: tax_kind
extensions.description: The kind of tax the rate is: VAT, GST, a sales tax, or another.

extensions.name: tiers
extensions.description: Tiered or volume pricing: { scheme (graduated | volume), tiers: [ { up_to (decimal string or null for the last tier), unit_amount { amount, currency }, flat_amount { amount, currency } } ] }.

extensions.name: trial_days
extensions.description: Free trial length in days granted when a subscription starts on this price.

extensions.name: usage_based
extensions.description: True when the quantity billed each period comes from metered usage rather than a fixed quantity.

extensions.name: exdates
extensions.description: RFC 5545 EXDATE: the occurrences of the series that are removed, as a comma-separated list of date-times.

extensions.name: rdates
extensions.description: RFC 5545 RDATE: extra occurrences added to the series, as a comma-separated list of date-times.

extensions.name: recurrence_id
extensions.description: RFC 5545 RECURRENCE-ID on a modified occurrence: the original start of the instance this record overrides; the series master is found by the shared ical:uid identifier.

extensions.name: reminders
extensions.description: Alarms before the event: { overrides: [ { method (popup, email), minutes_before (int) } ] }; absent means the calendar's default.

extensions.name: transparency
extensions.description: RFC 5545 TRANSP: whether the event blocks time (opaque) or not (transparent).

extensions.name: visibility
extensions.description: RFC 5545 CLASS: who may see the details.

extensions.name: image
extensions.description: The id of the File holding the product image.

extensions.name: annual_revenue
extensions.description: Annual revenue as Money { amount, currency }, as reported or estimated.

extensions.name: deal_source
extensions.description: Where this deal came from: the channel, campaign or referral that produced the opportunity. Named deal_source because the envelope's source object holds import provenance.

extensions.name: employees
extensions.description: Number of employees; a band from the source (1-10, 11-50) is kept in source.payload.

extensions.name: industry
extensions.description: The organization's industry in the workspace's own vocabulary; every CRM ships a different picklist.

extensions.name: lifecycle_stage
extensions.description: Where this person stands in the marketing and sales lifecycle, from subscriber to evangelist (the HubSpot stages, snake_case). A lead is a Person with lifecycle_stage lead; there is no Lead model.

extensions.name: lifecycle_stage
extensions.description: Where this organization stands in the marketing and sales lifecycle, from subscriber to evangelist.

extensions.name: line_items
extensions.description: The products on the deal before a quote or invoice exists: an object { lines: [ { product (a Product id), description, quantity (decimal string), unit_price { amount, currency } } ] }. Quantities and prices belong on the Invoice once one exists.

extensions.name: lost_reason
extensions.description: Why the deal was lost, in the team's own words or vocabulary.

extensions.name: source
extensions.description: Where this person came from: the channel or campaign that produced the contact (organic search, referral, event, paid social).

extensions.name: won_reason
extensions.description: Why the deal was won, in the team's own words or vocabulary.

extensions.name: received_at
extensions.description: When the receiving system accepted the message (the Received trace, Gmail internalDate, Graph receivedDateTime); sent_at orders the thread, this records delivery.

extensions.name: references
extensions.description: The RFC 5322 References header as written: the Message-IDs of the thread's ancestors, space-separated, for rebuilding threads of imported mail.

extensions.name: kind
extensions.description: What kind of group this is in the organization chart.

extensions.name: lead
extensions.description: The id of the Member who leads the team; the envelope's owner is the accountable operator of the record itself.

extensions.name: parent
extensions.description: The id of the parent Team in the hierarchy.

extensions.name: cc
extensions.description: People copied on the whole ticket rather than on single messages: { participants: [ Participant ] }.

extensions.name: first_responded_at
extensions.description: When the team first replied to the requester; the start of SLA reporting.

extensions.name: kind
extensions.description: The ticket type in the source's vocabulary: question, incident, problem, task, feedback, or a workspace's own.

extensions.name: parent
extensions.description: The id of the parent Ticket (a problem this incident belongs to, a tracker, a follow-up source).

extensions.name: satisfaction
extensions.description: The requester's rating after resolution: { rating (int, 1 to 5), comment }.

extensions.name: estimate
extensions.description: The effort estimate as an ISO 8601 duration; points and other units stay in source.payload.

extensions.name: rank
extensions.description: Manual ordering key within a view; lexicographic.

extensions.name: recurrence
extensions.description: An RFC 5545 RRULE for a task that recurs on completion; natural-language rules are translated or kept in source.payload.

extensions.name: start
extensions.description: When work is planned to start.

content.name: public reads published documents in public collections

core.name: end user reads and updates own person
end user comments on own person

support.name: end user reads and creates own tickets
end user reads messages about own tickets
end user reads shared notes about own tickets
end user sends messages about own tickets
